title: Boris Becker’s 1989 U.S. Open trophy sells for $357,456 in rare Grand Slam trophy auction
content:
The 1989 U.S. Open men’s singles championship trophy won by Boris Becker sold for $357,456 through The Tennis Auction on Sunday night. It’s one of the highest-priced pieces of tennis memorabilia ever sold publicly.

According to the auction house, it’s the only known U.S. Open men’s singles championship trophy from the Open era to ever hit the public market. Becker won the trophy by beating Ivan Lendl in the final, giving the German his only U.S. Open title and his fourth of six Grand Slam crowns.

The trophy originally resided, on loan from Becker, at the International Tennis Hall of Fame Museum in Newport, R.I. It later emerged publicly only as a result of the champion’s well-documented bankruptcy proceedings in 2019.

Becker was found guilty on four charges related to his bankruptcy case, which included illegally failing to hand over assets and trophies that were sought to repay his debts. Originally sentenced to 30 months in April 2022, the former No. 1-ranked player in the world served about eight months in prison.

Matt Cashin, founder of Prestige Memorabilia and The Tennis Auction, said Becker’s 1989 U.S. Open trophy was auctioned off in 2019 in connection to the bankruptcy case, with the consignor buying it originally for around $190,000. Cashin estimated the trophy would sell this time for around $250,000, meaning the sale jumped more than $100,000 higher than expected.

“It’s hard to imagine that (another Grand Slam trophy hits the market) for a while just because these players never want to part with their trophies,” Cashin said. “It’s like the grails of their career. And so it was definitely an unusual circumstance with Becker having to part with it. So definitely a really rare opportunity we had.”

The highest-priced publicly sold tennis item came in late January when the racket Novak Djokovic used during the 2012 Australian Open final, when he beat Rafael Nadal in the longest Grand Slam final in history, sold for $540,000. This Becker trophy sale doubled the highest-priced item ever sold on The Tennis Auction platform, with the previous high being $173,066 for a Carlos Alcaraz autographed racket he used during the 2023 Wimbledon final.
